thread:
IncidentBot: Pager triggered — Priority: P2 — private cluster 'acme-prod-eu' autoscaler failing to create GPU nodes (provider API rate limits + bootstrap timeouts). Rule: private.cluster.autoscale.error. Link: https://redwood.incidents/1729000001 :rotating_light:

samir: taking pager. seeing rapid queue growth on inference-queue-acme, lots of Pending pods. customer impact?

cs-jordan: Acme reports timeouts and 429/503s on live inference. They pushed a canary at 10:18 UTC and error rate jumped to ~50% for that traffic slice. Ticket RED-3214 created.

samir: looking at autoscaler logs — scale attempts hit provider 429 then backoff. posting quick snippets:

samir: ```
$ kubectl -n acme get pods -o wide | grep Pending | wc -l
1423

# describe shows ContainerCreating and FailedScheduling due to no nodes
kubectl describe nodepool acme-gpu-pool
# autoscaler: ScaleUp request failed: provider API 429 TooManyRequests
# subsequent bootstrap timeouts: node did not become Ready within 15m
```

priya: control plane events show: "autoscaler: ScaleUp blocked: providerRateLimit" then repeated "node bootstrap timed out after 15m". Possible culprits: provider rate limits + customer AMI that takes long to init (large init hooks).

raj: can we do any manual remediation? try another AZ or a different image type? fallback to smaller models to reduce pressure?

samir: manual scale via provider console also hitting 429s. I'm going to enable routing fallback to hosted-small for a portion of traffic to reduce load while we recover. Executing runbook step now.

samir: Runbook executed: /runbooks/private-autoscale-fallback -> routing change to send 20% of acme traffic to hosted-small. Command:
```json
{"action":"route","customer":"acme","percent":20,"target":"hosted-small"}
```

elena: taking over in 10m from Samir for the next on-call cycle. Current queue: ~12k requests backlog, avg wait ~48s, error rate ~38%. Manual provisioning ETA if provider quota clears ~25-40m.

samir: also purged stale KV cache prefixes to reduce memory pressure and request size. That shaved tail latency slightly.

priya: found registry errors in node init: customer uses a custom AMI with heavy cloud-init hooks + large docker layers. If we can provision with a standard Redwood GPU image for emergency nodes, bootstrap will be much faster, but needs customer's ok.

cs-jordan: pinged Acme for temporary AMI override; they replied OK for emergency override for 30 minutes.

elena: starting manual node group with standard image in eu-west-1 (to bypass custom AMI overhead). Command run:
```sh
providerctl create-node --region eu-west-1 --type p4 --image standard-gpu-2026 --count 4 --tags "temp-override=acme-emergency"
```
Job started (job id 98531).

IncidentBot: update — node group creation initiated, initial 2 nodes registered at 10:42 UTC, 2 nodes pending.

raj: autoscaler remains blocked by provider rate-limit for automated attempts; manual path is working slower but at least we get nodes. Long-term: provider retry/backoff policy needs tuning.

elena: nodes joining cluster: kubelet Ready on 2 nodes, pods scheduling and pulling caches. Queue dropped 12k -> 4.2k within 12 minutes. Routing still at 20% fallback. Error rate down to ~12% for the customer canary.

cs-jordan: customer degraded but acceptable for now. We opened postmortem RED-3214 and created a follow-up for quota/warm pool discussion.

priya: proposed next steps:
- short: relax autoscaler backoff and add small jitter to provider retries; pre-warm images for enterprise tenants; make AMI override documented in runbook.
- medium: multi-AZ provisioning fallback and reserve small burst capacity for committed customers.
- long: quota monitoring + automated pre-reserve when predicted spike.

elena: handing back to Samir for drafting postmortem and runbook updates. Samir: ack, will draft and link the postmortem.

samir: timeline + notes posted to incident doc: https://redwood.incidents/docs/1729000001. Closing pager signal now but keeping thread open for postmortem comments. :white_check_mark:
